metadata.title: `torch.max` does not create a named tuple if applied to a subclass

bug_description:
## 🐛 Bug



In PyTorch 1.7 on Ubuntu 20.04, `torch.max` does not create a named tuple if applied to a subclass, although the docs say it should be.



```

import torch

class _T(torch.Tensor): ...

x = torch.tensor([1,2]).as_subclass(_T)

torch.max(x, dim=0)

```



That returns



    (tensor(2), tensor(1))



It should return a named tuple.



cc @hameerabbasi @rgommers @mruberry

trigger_conditions.condition: Calling Tensor operators on Tensor subclass instances created through as_subclass, causing inconsistent return types or dispatch behavior compared with regular Tensor inputs.
